claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite a 1.8 percentage point miss in a named enterprise refund workflow segment, with legal review on disclosure still open.
specific_concerns: The cited policy text makes materiality turn on whether the weakness affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; the actor summary itself says the affected workflow is named in a renewal success plan.
The actor summary says legal review on required disclosure is still open, which leaves a required policy predicate unresolved at decision time.

The policy note described in the packet says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch; no approved risk acceptance or final disclosure evidence is identified.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure/materiality requirement.

The reliance on the affected segment being only 4% of projected first-month traffic conflicts with the policy text stating low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review are involved.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant based on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results alone.
That public model-card guidance and public AI risk guidance are sufficient support for an internal launch certification decision when an internal policy predicate remains unresolved.
That the 4% projected traffic figure is enough to treat the issue as immaterial for certification purposes.
That the conclusion to certify can be defended without evidence of either final disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the enterprise refund workflow gap must be disclosed before launch.
Provide the actual disclosure artifact, if issued, covering the named workflow limitation.
Provide any approved risk acceptance that explicitly covers this limitation for launch.
Provide the underlying evidence showing whether the affected workflow is a contractual customer segment or otherwise a named launch use case under policy.
Provide the source document for the renewal success plan and how the workflow is referenced there.
Provide the exact launch certification checklist or approval record showing how the materiality predicate was closed.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the limitation was either resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Treat unresolved legal review on a named use case as a material gap against certification support.
Do not let aggregate readiness or low traffic share override explicit materiality policy language.
Require a direct evidentiary link from the cited policy predicate to the certification decision record.
